title: Beta cohort check-in — Console Suggestions (Optimize)
summary: HelioDesk shared early feedback on the Console Suggestions (beta). They viewed ~11 suggestions across two routes and trialed a caching-related config change outside the product (since beta is read-only). They observed a smaller realized savings than the UI estimate and want clearer explanation of: baseline window, what assumptions drive the estimate, and how confidence relates to risk. Key requested UX tweaks: show the baseline period + traffic sample size, show “last updated” for telemetry, provide a clearer breakdown of savings attribution (batching vs caching) and guardrails (what could increase latency). Redwood noted week-to-week estimate variance is expected when traffic mix shifts and when cache hit-rate is lower than the model assumption; Logan will investigate a possible metering/baseline mismatch for one route. Team aligned on next steps and a follow-up after Redwood reviews telemetry and provides a written explanation HelioDesk can share internally.
topics: Adoption status: which routes have suggestions, which were acted on manually
Mismatch between estimated savings and realized savings
Estimate explainability: baseline window, sample size, confidence intervals
Risk labeling: what “High” means and what concrete signals drove it
UI/UX tweaks requested for beta (filters, copy, last-updated, export/share)
Telemetry freshness and missing/insufficient data cases
action_items: Logan Wright - Investigate baseline vs metering mismatch on /chat-support route (compare token metering dataset vs suggestion basis fields) - Due 2026-02-06
Evan Scott - Send HelioDesk a short write-up explaining how caching savings is computed (baseline window, assumed hit-rate, latency tradeoffs) - Due 2026-02-05
Miguel Santos - Schedule 30-min follow-up with Priya/Elena after investigation; include updated screenshots and recommended interpretation guidance - Due 2026-02-10
Aditya Rao - Capture UX requests (baseline window, sample size, last updated, export/share) and log in beta feedback tracker for Console team - Due 2026-02-04
next_steps: Redwood to validate telemetry freshness and confirm whether savings estimate over-counted for one route
HelioDesk to share internal before/after cost snapshots (per 1M tokens) and any config changes they made
Follow-up meeting next week to review findings and decide whether to expand beta to additional routes
transcript:
Meeting: Beta cohort check-in — Console Suggestions (Optimize)
Recorded: 2026-02-03 17:00 UTC
Duration: 46 min
Attendees:
- Miguel Santos (Redwood, CSM)
- Evan Scott (Redwood, Solutions Engineer)
- Logan Wright (Redwood, Telemetry/Analytics)
- Aditya Rao (Redwood, Product - Optimize)
- Priya Desai (HelioDesk, Platform Eng Lead)
- Mark Chen (HelioDesk, Staff ML Eng)
- Elena Alvarez (HelioDesk, FinOps)

---

[00:00] Miguel Santos: Alright, cool. Thanks everyone for making time. This is our beta cohort check-in for the Suggestions view in Console. Goal today is basically: what you tried, what looked confusing, what we should fix before we widen the cohort.

[00:18] Priya Desai: Yep. We’ve got some notes. Elena especially has… feelings about the savings numbers.

[00:23] Elena Alvarez: (laughs) Feelings is accurate.

[00:26] Evan Scott: Great. We want the brutal truth.

[00:30] Aditya Rao: And just as a reminder, this is still read-only, so anything you applied you did manually, right?

[00:36] Mark Chen: Yeah, we did manual changes in our route config. We didn’t wait for one-click apply, obviously.

[00:43] Miguel Santos: Perfect. Maybe start with adoption. Priya, which routes did you look at?

[00:50] Priya Desai: So, we have two main Redwood routes that matter for cost. One is our customer support chat endpoint, internal name is /chat-support. Second is /agent-drafts, which does longer generations. Both are hosted right now, not dedicated.

[01:08] Priya Desai: In Suggestions, we saw, I think, 11 total, but really 3 were relevant. Two were caching-related and one was batching/“continuous batching” tuning.

[01:21] Evan Scott: Okay.

[01:22] Priya Desai: We clicked into the caching one for /chat-support, and it said estimated savings like… 22%? And then monthly dollars, it was like $8k-ish. Something like that.

[01:34] Elena Alvarez: It showed a range, but it was still… big.

[01:38] Miguel Santos: Got it. And then what did you actually see after the change?

[01:43] Elena Alvarez: We saw like 6 to 9%. Definitely not 22.

[01:49] Mark Chen: Closer to 8% on our side. And we did it for about four days.

[01:55] Aditya Rao: That’s helpful. Can we dig into how you measured realized savings?

[02:00] Elena Alvarez: We basically compared the Redwood invoice line item, tokens billed, divided by our request volume. Also our internal dashboard. It’s not perfect but directionally.

[02:12] Logan Wright: When you say invoice, are you looking at daily usage exports or just end-of-month?

[02:17] Elena Alvarez: Daily usage export.

[02:20] Logan Wright: Okay.

[02:21] Evan Scott: And was traffic mix stable across those four days? Like prompt length, completion length, model version pinned, that kind of thing.

[02:30] Mark Chen: Model version pinned, yes. Mix… not stable. Mondays are always weird for us.

[02:36] Priya Desai: Yeah, we had a product launch on Tuesday. It shifted a bunch of support volume.

[02:43] Elena Alvarez: But the suggestion didn’t say “only valid if your traffic is normal.” It just said estimated savings.

[02:49] Aditya Rao: Fair critique. The intent is “based on recent baseline.” But we should make the baseline window explicit.

[02:57] Miguel Santos: This is the exact kind of thing we want to tighten in the UI.

[03:02] Logan Wright: The current estimate uses the last 7 days baseline for that route/model/region combo. If your Tuesday was a spike with different token distribution, that can throw off realized vs estimated.

[03:16] Elena Alvarez: Wait, so it’s seven days trailing, always?

[03:18] Logan Wright: For v1, yes. It’s basically a rolling window with some smoothing. And we compute an expected impact for caching using assumed cache hit rate lift, derived from similar workloads + your observed prefix repetition.

[03:34] Mark Chen: The detail drawer had “basis of estimate” but it’s kind of… thin. It showed a couple numbers but not enough for me to sanity check.

[03:42] Priya Desai: Yeah, it had like “baseline tokens” and “estimated hit-rate.” I didn’t see sample size, like number of requests.

[03:49] Evan Scott: That’s a good request. Right now we show token counts, not request counts, because token metering is what we trust most. But we can add request sample size too.

[03:58] Aditya Rao: And baseline dates. Like “Jan 27 to Feb 2”. That’s easy.

[04:05] Elena Alvarez: And “last updated.” Because sometimes it changes week to week and we’re like, did we do something, or did you do something?

[04:12] Miguel Santos: Yeah. We’ve heard that from another beta account as well.

[04:17] Evan Scott: Can we pause on the realized savings being 8% vs 22%. Mark, what change did you apply? Specifically.

[04:26] Mark Chen: We increased caching for system prompt prefix. We basically normalized the system prompt and moved some dynamic bits into user content, plus we adjusted whatever header you call it for the cache key. I might be mixing terms.

[04:39] Evan Scott: That sounds right. For Redwood, it’s more like “prefix cache eligibility” and your prompt structure determines it. There’s no single header, but there’s policy.

[04:49] Mark Chen: Right, sorry. We followed your docs from earlier. Also we tried increasing the “min prefix tokens” threshold.

[04:57] Logan Wright: If you increased min prefix tokens too much, you might have reduced cacheable traffic. Like you can drop hit rate.

[05:05] Mark Chen: Possibly.

[05:07] Priya Desai: Also, we have a ton of unique customer context. So I’m not sure we can ever get to those assumed hit rates.

[05:15] Aditya Rao: That’s exactly why we included confidence intervals. But we haven’t exposed confidence clearly in the list.

[05:23] Elena Alvarez: It shows “confidence: medium” sometimes, but it’s not clear how that relates to “risk: low” or “risk: medium.” Like we had one that was low risk but… medium confidence. What does that mean? It’s confusing.

[05:37] Miguel Santos: Yeah, we’ve been debating whether confidence should be separate or folded into risk.

[05:42] Evan Scott: Today, risk is more about “could this hurt you.” Like latency or quality regression potential. Confidence is “how sure we are about savings.”

[05:51] Mark Chen: Those are different axes. I like that, but only if you explain it.

[05:56] Aditya Rao: Makes sense.

[05:58] Priya Desai: Another thing: the caching suggestion said “Low risk” which we interpreted as, okay, safe. But it didn’t mention potential latency impact due to cache lookup overhead or any of that. Then later we saw p95 move slightly.

[06:11] Evan Scott: Cache lookup overhead should be minimal; usually caching helps latency. But, if it changes batching behavior or you’re pushing different sequence lengths, you can get weirdness.

[06:22] Mark Chen: Yeah we saw p95 up like 15ms. Not huge.

[06:26] Evan Scott: That’s within noise usually, but we should call out assumptions.

[06:31] Logan Wright: Also, if your traffic changed, p95 can move for reasons unrelated.

[06:36] Elena Alvarez: This is why we want the UI to say what it’s assuming. Like “assuming cache hit rate improves from X to Y.” It kind of said that but it was buried.

[06:46] Aditya Rao: Got it. We can pull the assumptions into a more prominent section.

[06:50] Miguel Santos: On the mismatch, Logan, do you have any suspicion of actual bugs? Or mostly baseline drift?

[06:56] Logan Wright: I want to check one thing. We had a known issue a couple weeks back with double counting when both caching and batching were applicable. That should be fixed now, but depending on when the suggestion was generated, it might still show inflated numbers.

[07:12] Mark Chen: The suggestion we saw was created… I think it said “generated 9 days ago.”

[07:17] Logan Wright: Okay that’s a clue.

[07:19] Priya Desai: Wait, it’s generated and then it just sits there?

[07:22] Logan Wright: It refreshes, but some basis fields can be stale if telemetry was delayed. We’re adding a “stale estimate detection” alert, but I don’t think it’s surfaced to UI yet.

[07:34] Elena Alvarez: That would be a big improvement. Like, show a banner “data may be stale” if it’s older than 24 hours.

[07:41] Aditya Rao: That’s on our list.

[07:43] Evan Scott: Also helpful would be: “why no suggestions.” Did you see any empty states?

[07:49] Priya Desai: For /agent-drafts it showed “insufficient telemetry” for a while, even though there’s traffic.

[07:56] Mark Chen: It’s lower volume but still active.

[07:59] Logan Wright: That might be because we don’t have enough sample size to do a stable baseline. There’s a threshold for tokens + requests.

[08:08] Priya Desai: The UI just said “insufficient data.” It didn’t say “we need X requests per day.”

[08:14] Evan Scott: We should add more specific guidance. Otherwise it feels broken.

[08:20] Miguel Santos: Elena, can you talk through the finance angle? Like what you need to show internally.

[08:26] Elena Alvarez: Yeah. If I’m going to take this to our VP, I need to say: “We changed X, it saved Y, we’re confident.” The Suggestions view is close, but I need something I can paste into a doc. Like an export, or even a “copy summary” button.

[08:45] Elena Alvarez: And I need the “basis of estimate” to include the period, sample size, and ideally a confidence range. Right now the range is there but doesn’t explain why the range is that wide.

[08:58] Aditya Rao: We can add a “what drives the range” section. That’s likely variance in workload + uncertainty in hit rate.

[09:06] Mark Chen: Also quality risk. You show “risk: high” on a batching suggestion for /agent-drafts. But it didn’t tell me why it’s high.

[09:15] Evan Scott: Was that the one about increasing max batch size?

[09:18] Mark Chen: Yes.

[09:20] Priya Desai: It said something like “increase batching to improve GPU utilization.” Then “High risk.” We didn’t do it because… high risk.

[09:27] Mark Chen: But what risk? Latency? Quality? Timeouts?

[09:31] Aditya Rao: In our taxonomy, high risk can mean “low latency headroom” or “workload variance is high,” which means batching might push you over SLO.

[09:41] Logan Wright: For long generations like /agent-drafts, batching can increase tail latency if the batch gets stuck behind a long sequence.

[09:49] Mark Chen: That’s the concrete explanation I wanted in the UI.

[09:53] Miguel Santos: Totally fair. The detail drawer should have rationale bullets. I think the new build has those, but maybe not rolled to your tenant?

[10:02] Priya Desai: We didn’t see bullets. We saw a sentence.

[10:06] Aditya Rao: Okay, that’s actionable.

[10:09] Evan Scott: Another UX question: list view filtering. Did you use filters?

[10:14] Priya Desai: Yes. Filter by route was good. But we wanted filter by region too, because we have us-east and eu-west. The suggestions seemed aggregated.

[10:26] Logan Wright: Today it’s per route/model/region under the hood, but the UI might default to “all regions” if you don’t pick one.

[10:34] Priya Desai: That’s confusing. “All regions” is not a thing for us, because costs differ.

[10:39] Evan Scott: We can make the default explicit, like a chip “All regions” and require selection for region-specific routes.

[10:47] Elena Alvarez: Also costs in EU are different, so savings in dollars should show region.

[10:53] Aditya Rao: Agreed.

[10:55] Miguel Santos: Let’s dig into the savings calc quickly, just enough so you can interpret it. Logan, can you summarize what numbers feed the 22%?

[11:03] Logan Wright: Sure. For caching suggestions, we compute baseline cost per 1M tokens for the route and the observed prefix repetition ratio. Then we estimate incremental cache hit-rate improvement from the suggested change. Savings is basically baseline_cost * expected_reduction_in_compute_tokens, adjusted for cache overhead and some guardrail factors.

[11:26] Logan Wright: If your repetition ratio is lower than expected, or if the prompt structure change didn’t actually increase prefix stability, then realized will be lower.

[11:36] Mark Chen: That’s probably us. A lot of our context is unique.

[11:40] Elena Alvarez: But the estimate was still high.

[11:43] Logan Wright: That’s why I want to check if the baseline was computed correctly. There’s one failure mode where tokens are attributed to the route incorrectly if your route tags changed.

[11:54] Priya Desai: We did rename the route last month.

[11:57] Logan Wright: Okay. That can cause a baseline mismatch if the pipeline didn’t map old route_id to new route_id in the rolling window.

[12:06] Evan Scott: That could inflate or deflate.

[12:08] Logan Wright: Yeah.

[12:10] Miguel Santos: Great catch. Logan, can you take that as an investigation item?

[12:14] Logan Wright: Yes, I’ll look at /chat-support route id history.

[12:18] Aditya Rao: And we’ll add UI messaging for “route recently changed” maybe.

[12:23] Priya Desai: That would be useful.

[12:26] (crosstalk)
[12:26] Elena Alvarez: Also—
[12:27] Mark Chen: Another thing—

[12:28] Miguel Santos: Go ahead Elena.

[12:31] Elena Alvarez: The savings estimate changed between Friday and Monday. Same suggestion, different dollars. That freaks people out.

[12:39] Logan Wright: That’s because baseline window moved. But we can show “baseline updated” and what changed.

[12:45] Evan Scott: Maybe even show a small sparkline or “previous estimate”?

[12:49] Aditya Rao: We have to be careful not to add too much noise, but yeah, at least “last computed at” and “baseline period.”

[12:58] Mark Chen: Another UI tweak: I want to see savings in $/1M tokens more prominently than monthly dollars. Monthly depends on volume assumptions.

[13:08] Aditya Rao: That’s a great point. We show both, but we can let you choose default. We’ve heard FinOps prefers per-unit.

[13:16] Elena Alvarez: Yes. Monthly is good for execs but per-unit is what we optimize.

[13:22] Miguel Santos: On the question of trust: would a confidence interval help? Like “expected savings 10–25%, p50 18%”?

[13:31] Elena Alvarez: Yes, but only if you explain it’s not guaranteed.

[13:34] Evan Scott: Our copy currently says “estimated” not “guaranteed,” but we can make that stronger.

[13:39] Priya Desai: And please don’t hide behind “estimated.” Tell me why.

[13:44] Aditya Rao: Totally.

[13:46] Miguel Santos: Ok. Let’s talk about the “apply” workflow request. I know it’s read-only now, but do you want it? Or is it scary.

[13:55] Priya Desai: We want it eventually, but with guardrails. Like, apply to a canary route first, easy rollback.

[14:03] Mark Chen: Yeah. And I want to see the exact config diff before applying.

[14:08] Elena Alvarez: And we need audit logs, who applied what. For compliance.

[14:14] Evan Scott: That aligns with our phase 2 plan. Right now we’re trying to make the recommendations itself trustworthy first.

[14:21] Miguel Santos: Good.

[14:23] Aditya Rao: Another quick check: any security concerns with the Suggestions view? It surfaces cost and usage-derived data.

[14:31] Priya Desai: For us, as long as RBAC is correct. We only want platform/admin to see it.

[14:37] Elena Alvarez: Yes, ideally it’s only the right roles.

[14:41] Miguel Santos: Noted. RBAC is already in place but we’ll double-check your tenant roles.

[14:46] Evan Scott: Can we circle back to /agent-drafts “insufficient telemetry”? Mark, what volume roughly.

[14:53] Mark Chen: Maybe 2k requests/day, but long outputs.

[14:57] Logan Wright: That should be enough, unless the route label isn’t being attached on some traffic.

[15:03] Priya Desai: We might be missing route tags in one service. We had a migration.

[15:07] Logan Wright: That would explain it. The suggestion service only sees what’s tagged.

[15:12] Evan Scott: If you want, we can provide a quick query / checklist to validate route tagging.

[15:18] Priya Desai: Yes, please.

[15:20] Miguel Santos: Evan can send that.

[15:22] Aditya Rao: Also UI could say “we’re seeing telemetry but not enough with route tag.” More specific.

[15:28] Elena Alvarez: That would reduce support tickets.

[15:31] Miguel Santos: Yeah.

[15:33] (brief pause)

[15:35] Miguel Santos: Anything else on UX? Filtering, sorting, copy.

[15:39] Priya Desai: Sorting by “biggest savings first” was helpful. But it sometimes felt wrong, because high savings were high risk, and then you just scroll past.

[15:48] Mark Chen: A combined sort like “savings adjusted by confidence” would be interesting.

[15:54] Aditya Rao: We’ve talked about “expected value” sort. Might be for later, but we can consider it.

[16:01] Elena Alvarez: At least let me filter out High risk.

[16:05] Evan Scott: That exists, right? Risk filter.

[16:07] Priya Desai: It exists but it was not obvious.

[16:10] Evan Scott: Okay, we can make that more prominent.

[16:13] Miguel Santos: On the estimate mismatch, just to confirm: you made prompt changes + min prefix token change, then saw about 8% improvement. Do you recall what the suggestion expected?

[16:25] Mark Chen: It expected cache hit-rate to go from like 0.12 to 0.28. Something like that.

[16:31] Logan Wright: That’s a big jump.

[16:33] Mark Chen: We probably didn’t get that.

[16:35] Priya Desai: Also, our traffic is bursty. When we have bursts, caching is less effective because context changes.

[16:44] Logan Wright: Bursty traffic can also change batching effectiveness. It’s a key input to confidence.

[16:51] Aditya Rao: This is where we want to show “workload variance” as a rationale.

[16:57] Elena Alvarez: Please do. Even if it’s a bullet: “High variance week over week.”

[17:02] Miguel Santos: Yep.

[17:04] Evan Scott: One more: do you want the suggestion to include “how to implement” steps? Like, not just “increase caching,” but “move dynamic fields after stable prefix” with examples.

[17:14] Mark Chen: Yes, but keep it short. Link out to docs. Don’t put a textbook in the drawer.

[17:20] Priya Desai: A small snippet or example would be great.

[17:24] Aditya Rao: That’s good feedback.

[17:27] Miguel Santos: Okay, I’m going to shift into recap mode soon, but Logan, can you confirm what you’ll investigate specifically.

[17:35] Logan Wright: I’ll check route_id change history for /chat-support, validate that baseline window is pulling the right metering series, and confirm the suggestion wasn’t generated pre-fix for double counting. If it was, we should regenerate it.

[17:53] Elena Alvarez: And can you tell us if the 22% was just wrong.

[17:56] Logan Wright: Yes. If it was, we’ll say that plainly.

[18:00] Miguel Santos: Appreciate it.

[18:02] Evan Scott: I’ll send a short “how caching savings works” explanation and also a route-tagging validation checklist.

[18:10] Priya Desai: Great.

[18:12] Aditya Rao: And I’ll log UI feedback: baseline dates, sample size, last updated, region clarity, and more explicit risk rationale bullets.

[18:22] Miguel Santos: Perfect. Any other concerns? Competitors, internal alternatives.

[18:27] Priya Desai: We’re also looking at self-hosting vLLM for some workloads, but we don’t want to build a ton of infra. This Suggestions thing is actually what would keep us on Redwood if it’s trustworthy.

[18:39] Elena Alvarez: Yeah, if it helps us systematically reduce spend, that’s value.

[18:43] Evan Scott: Understood.

[18:45] Miguel Santos: Great. We’ll follow up by end of week with findings. Let’s schedule a 30-min follow-up next Tuesday or Wednesday.

[18:53] Priya Desai: Tuesday works.

[18:55] Miguel Santos: Cool, I’ll send.

[18:57] (call continues with minor scheduling and wrap-up)

[19:05] Miguel Santos: Last thing—if you can share your before/after per 1M tokens chart, even a screenshot, that helps us compare.

[19:12] Elena Alvarez: Yep, I’ll send it in email.

[19:15] Miguel Santos: Awesome. Thanks everyone.

---

Auto-generated Questions:
- What baseline window is used for savings estimates, and how often do they refresh?
- How should users interpret confidence vs risk?
- How can users validate telemetry tagging when Suggestions shows “insufficient data”?

Auto-generated Action items:
- Logan to investigate route baseline/metering mismatch and potential stale suggestion generation.
- Evan to send caching savings methodology + route tagging checklist.
- Redwood team to consider UI additions: baseline period, sample size, last updated timestamp, clearer risk rationale, region clarity, export/share summary.
